name: Mayfair Himalayan Spa Resort
summary: The old Himalayan Hotel on Upper Cart Road, built as the home of the MacDonald family and now run by Mayfair as a spa resort. It is the most comfortable stay in Kalimpong, with heritage rooms in the original stone house and newer wings around it.
body: David Macdonald, who worked as interpreter on the 1904 British expedition to Tibet and later as British trade agent there, retired to Kalimpong and turned his family home into a guest house. Through the twentieth century it became a stop for mountaineers and travellers heading to Tibet and Everest. The MacDonald family ran it for generations before the Mayfair group took it over and rebuilt it as a resort.

The original house, with its wooden floors and fireplaces, keeps the heritage rooms. Newer blocks add deluxe rooms, a spa, a pool and a restaurant. It is a short drive from the haat bazaar and Durpin Hill, and rooms on the upper side look towards Kanchenjunga on clear mornings.
why: The best rooms and service in Kalimpong town
A building with real history tied to the Tibet trade
Spa, pool and good food after long village drives
Central enough to walk to the haat and the old bazaar

faqs.q: Is Mayfair Himalayan Spa Resort the same as the old Himalayan Hotel?
faqs.a: Yes. The resort grew out of the Himalayan Hotel, the former home of the MacDonald family on Upper Cart Road. Mayfair Hotels and Resorts took it over and added new wings, a spa and a pool, while keeping the old stone house as heritage rooms. Ask for a room in the original building if the history matters to you.

faqs.q: How far is it from the centre of Kalimpong?
faqs.a: It is on Upper Cart Road, roughly a kilometre from the haat bazaar and the main market. You can walk to the bazaar in 15–20 minutes, though the return is uphill. Durpin Hill and the Zang Dhok Palri monastery are about 15 minutes away by car, and Deolo Hill about 20 minutes.

faqs.q: Is it worth the price on a budget trip?
faqs.a: On a strict budget, no: a room costs roughly ₹12,000–22,000 a night, indicative, against ₹1,500–2,200 a person in a village homestay. It works well as a single comfort night at the end of a village circuit, when a hot bath and a spa are worth paying for. Weekday and off-season rates are often lower.

name: Morgan House (WBTDC)
summary: A stone colonial mansion on Durpin Hill, built in the 1930s by the jute merchant George Morgan and now run as a government tourist lodge by WBTDC. You pay a modest rate for high ceilings, lawns and a mountain view, with simple service.
body: Morgan House stands in large grounds on Durpin Hill, about 3 km from the town centre and close to the Zang Dhok Palri monastery. After independence it passed to the government, and the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation has run it as a tourist lodge for decades. Locals will tell you it is haunted; most guests only meet creaky floors and cold corridors.

Rooms vary a lot. The best are the large rooms in the old house with views of the Kanchenjunga range; others are plain. Food is simple Indian and Chinese from the lodge kitchen. Book through the WBTDC website and check recent reviews, since upkeep has varied over the years.
why: A real colonial house at a government lodge price
Quiet grounds on Durpin Hill with mountain views
Walking distance of Zang Dhok Palri monastery
Bookable online through WBTDC

faqs.q: Who built Morgan House in Kalimpong?
faqs.a: It was built in the 1930s by George Morgan, a British jute merchant, as a family house on Durpin Hill. After 1947 the property passed to the Government of India and later to the West Bengal government, and WBTDC runs it today as a tourist lodge. It is one of the best-known colonial buildings in Kalimpong.

It has a long local reputation as a haunted house, and the story is often repeated in travel writing. We know of no evidence for it. What guests do report is a large, old building that feels cold and echoing at night, especially in winter. Ask for a room in the main house if you want the atmosphere.

faqs.q: How do I book Morgan House?
faqs.a: Book online through the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation website, or at WBTDC offices in Kolkata and Siliguri. Rooms in the old house sell out first in October, April and May. Rates are indicative at about ₹3,000–6,500 a room per night, and meals are paid separately at the lodge restaurant.

name: WBFDC Lava Nature Resort
summary: Wooden cottages run by the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation on a forested slope at Lava. It is the closest thing to staying inside the forest without a tent, and the best base for Neora Valley.
body: The resort sits among tall trees just above Lava bazaar, with cottages spread up a steep slope. Mist rolls through most afternoons, and birds come right up to the verandas in the early morning. The forest office for Neora Valley permits is close by.

Facilities are simple: clean rooms, hot water at set times and a canteen that serves set meals. Order meals in advance. Some cottages are reached by long flights of steps, which matters for older travellers. Book on the WBFDC website, which usually opens bookings about three months ahead.
why: Forest setting right on the edge of Lava
Close to the Neora Valley permit office
Good early-morning birding from the grounds
Government rates that stay fair in peak season

faqs.q: How do I book the WBFDC resort at Lava?
faqs.a: Book online on the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation website, which usually opens dates about three months ahead, or at the WBFDC office in Kolkata. Peak weeks in October and May sell out quickly. Rates are indicative at about ₹1,500–3,500 a room per night, depending on the cottage. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the Lava nature resort suitable for older travellers?
faqs.a: Partly. The cottages with the best views are higher up the slope and reached by many steps, which can be hard on knees and for small children. Ask for a lower cottage when you book. Paths can be wet and mossy, so good shoes help, and a torch is useful after dark.

faqs.q: Is food available at the resort?
faqs.a: Yes, a canteen serves simple set meals: rice, dal, vegetables, eggs or chicken, and breakfast. There are few other places to eat close by, apart from small shops in Lava bazaar. Tell the canteen manager your meal times on arrival, and order early if you are leaving for Neora Valley before dawn.

name: Rishop village homestays
price_band: ₹1,500–2,200 per person per night with all meals
summary: Family-run homestays and small cottages in Rishop, many run by Sherpa and Lepcha families, with rooms facing the Kanchenjunga range. They are simple, warm and the main way to stay in the village.
body: Rishop has no large hotels. Instead, a few dozen families rent out rooms in their own houses or in wooden cottages beside them. Rooms are basic but clean, with thick quilts and, in better places, a geyser. Meals are home-cooked: rice, dal, local greens, eggs, chicken and, if you ask, momos or thukpa.

The best rooms face north-west towards Kanchenjunga. Ask about the view, the bathroom and heating when you book, since standards vary from house to house. Power cuts happen, so carry a torch and a power bank. Most hosts can arrange a car or a guide for the walk to Lava.
why: Wake up to the mountain view from your room
Home-cooked meals included in the price
Money goes straight to village families
Hosts know the forest paths and sunrise points

faqs.q: What does a Rishop homestay include?
faqs.a: Most include a room with an attached bathroom and all meals: breakfast, lunch or packed lunch, evening tea and dinner. Expect about ₹1,500–2,200 a person a night, indicative. Hot water may come by geyser or bucket. Heaters cost extra where they exist. Confirm what is included before you pay an advance.

faqs.q: Are Rishop homestays warm enough in winter?
faqs.a: Nights between December and February drop to around freezing, and houses are not centrally heated. Hosts give thick quilts, and some provide electric heaters for a fee. Bring thermals, a warm hat and socks for sleeping. A hot-water bottle helps. Ask about heaters when you book, since power cuts can switch them off.

faqs.q: Can I book Rishop homestays online?
faqs.a: Some are listed on booking sites, but many are booked by phone or through drivers and local agents. We book homestays we have checked for clean bathrooms and honest pricing. If you book yourself, ask for recent photos of the room and bathroom, and confirm the meal plan and the road access for your car.

name: Lolegaon village homestays
price_band: ₹1,400–2,000 per person per night with all meals
summary: Simple homestays run by Lepcha and Nepali families around Lolegaon and nearby Kafer. They put you within walking distance of the canopy walk and the Jhandi Dara sunrise road.
body: Lolegaon is a small Lepcha village on a ridge, and most stays are rooms in family houses or small cottages in the garden. Many have a view down the valley, and some face the Kanchenjunga range. Food is home-style and plentiful, often with vegetables from the family plot.

Standards vary, so ask about bathrooms, hot water and road access. The village is quiet after dark, with no restaurants to speak of, so all meals come from your host. Hosts can arrange an early car to Jhandi Dara and a guide for forest walks.
why: Close to the heritage forest and canopy walk
Quiet village with almost no traffic
Meals cooked by the family
Fair prices that include everything

faqs.q: How many nights should I stay in Lolegaon?
faqs.a: One night is enough for the canopy walk, the Jhandi Dara sunrise and a village stroll. Stay two if you want a full lazy day in the forest or are coming from Siliguri without breaking the journey. Many travellers combine one night in Lolegaon with one or two in Lava and Rishop.

faqs.q: Is there mobile signal in Lolegaon?
faqs.a: Signal is patchy. Jio and Airtel usually work in parts of the village, but can drop indoors or in bad weather. Some homestays have Wi-Fi that runs only when power is on. Download maps and confirm your onward car before you arrive, and tell family you may be out of reach for a night.

faqs.q: What do homestays in Lolegaon cost?
faqs.a: Expect roughly ₹1,400–2,000 a person per night including all meals, indicative. Rooms with the best views or new bathrooms cost a little more. Children often pay less. A car to Jhandi Dara at sunrise costs extra, typically ₹600–1,000 for the vehicle. Prices rise in October and during school holidays.

name: Sillery Gaon village homestays
price_band: ₹1,500–2,200 per person per night with all meals
summary: A cluster of family homestays in Sillery Gaon above Pedong, with rooms facing Kanchenjunga across the valleys. They are the only kind of stay in the village and the base for Ramitey Dara and Damsang.
body: Sillery Gaon is a small village of a few dozen houses on a ridge at about 1,830 m. Over the past fifteen years many families have added rooms or cottages for guests. Most rooms are simple wood or concrete with attached bathrooms, and the better ones have balconies facing the mountains.

Meals are cooked at home and eaten with the family or in a small dining room. The last stretch of road up from Pedong is narrow and steep, so check with your host before sending a large vehicle. Hosts arrange guides and cars for Ramitey Dara, Damsang Fort and Pedong.
why: Kanchenjunga views from many rooms
Short drive or walk to Ramitey Dara
Good base for Pedong and Damsang history
Easy to add to a Kalimpong or Silk Route trip

faqs.q: Can a car reach Sillery Gaon homestays?
faqs.a: Yes, but the road from Pedong is narrow, steep and partly rough, especially after rain. Small cars and local jeeps manage it; large tempo travellers often cannot reach the top. Your host may send a local jeep from Pedong. Check road conditions with them a day before, especially between June and September.

faqs.q: What is included in a Sillery Gaon homestay?
faqs.a: The usual plan includes a room with attached bathroom and all meals, from breakfast to dinner, plus evening tea. Expect about ₹1,500–2,200 a person a night, indicative. A guide to Ramitey Dara or a jeep to Damsang Fort is extra. Ask whether hot water is by geyser and whether heaters are available in winter.

faqs.q: Is Sillery Gaon good for families with children?
faqs.a: Yes, if the children are happy with simple rooms and quiet evenings. There is space to play in the village and easy walks. The road up is steep and winding, so carry motion sickness tablets. Keep an eye on small children at the viewpoints, which have long drops and few railings.
